questions.advice: Write a short statement you can give anyone who asks what you are working on. Set goals around what the reader gains, and focus less on the sell.

questions.title: How often you can publish
questions.prompt: How often can you publish for the next six months and keep it up? Think about your 15 to 20 weekly hours and Q-05.
questions.why: Revenue scenarios assume a steady publishing rhythm.
questions.advice: Consistent volume and frequency matter more than occasional bursts. Start with a pace you can hold.

files.text: Newest plan: a weekly beehiiv issue (you record Monday, approve Wednesday, it publishes Thursday) plus a LinkedIn edition every other week. Four older plans differ. Nothing has been published.
decide: Approve that rhythm, or set a lower one that fits your hours.

questions.title: Where your email contacts came from
questions.prompt: Where did your email contacts come from, and which of them have agreed to get a newsletter from you? If you are not sure, say so.
questions.why: Q-01 asks for the contact count. This tells Miah how many can be invited and how.
questions.advice: Ask for permission clearly, tell people what they will get and how often, and make unsubscribing one click. Do not email an address if you do not know where it came from.
questions.caution: Rules on bulk email depend on where you and your readers live. Ask a qualified advisor if you are unsure. This page is not legal advice.

files.text: No list for your newsletter exists in any file.
decide: Start from zero, or name the list and how consent was given.
Agree: no imports from LinkedIn connections or old address books without opt-in.

questions.title: How you will measure the newsletter
questions.prompt: Which measures matter to you most? For example, subscriber growth, clicks, replies, unsubscribes or new conversations.
questions.why: It feeds Q-10, the engagement-count convention for public use.
questions.advice: Set the measures before you send. Prefer click-through, deliverability and bounce rate over open rates, and tie results to business outcomes.

files.text: The files agree: report inquiries, interviews, bookings and revenue first and engagement second, with review gates at months 2, 3, 4 and 6.
decide: Approve that order and the gates.

questions.title: Sending address and platform setup
questions.prompt: Should the newsletter send from your own domain, such as rbolmsted.com, or from the platform's domain? Who will handle the domain settings?
questions.why: A custom sending domain needs setup so mail is trusted. This overlaps with Miah's Cloudflare work.
questions.advice: Set up email authentication (SPF and DKIM) so your mail is verified as yours. Start with small sends to your best contacts, then build up volume.

decide: beehiiv, or the comparison first?
Send from @transformingdata.llc, or from a subdomain of rbolmsted.com?

questions.title: First issue
questions.prompt: What is the one message of the first issue? Add a draft subject line of about 50 characters or fewer, and a one-line preview of about 100 characters.
questions.why: Nothing is sent. This only drafts the first issue for your review.
questions.advice: One message per email. Trim the copy, make the action clear, test how it looks on a phone and with images off, and run a small test before a full send.
